bio.text: Jacques Callot, the first inventive international printmaker, culled [something] from everywhere and imparted something to all subsequent etching and [engraving].

source.author: A. Hyatt Mayor
source.title: Prints & People: A Social History of Printed Pictures
source.publisher: The Metropolitan Museum of Art (Internet Archive scan)

bio.text: Jacques Callot, of Nancy (b. 1592), happily knew his mind better and earlier than his parents, who had intended him for the Church.

source.author: Arthur M. Hind
source.title: A Short History of Engraving and Etching

bio.text: From a life of some 43 years, more than 2000 drawings survive, studying every stroke of over 1400 prints. Such strict application never tired a vivacity so inexhaustible that he could copy his most complex etchings on second coppers with no loss of freshness.

source.author: A. Hyatt Mayor
source.title: Prints & People: A Social History of Printed Pictures
source.publisher: The Metropolitan Museum of Art (Internet Archive scan)
